decisions.evidence: R1 maker (spec gate) explicitly asserted a scope boundary contradicting the reference: 'No automatic page-metadata fetching — no auto-fetched real titles, favicons, or previews (titles are typed or derived from the address)'. R1 client rejected it: 'Saving a link should automatically collect its title, description, favicon, and preview image. I should be able to edit the title and description.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Divergence established from the presentation's explicit exclusion of REF-BM-02/03; client negates the stated 'no fetch' behaviour and supplies the reference-conforming requirement.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker spec treated duplicates only as an edge case ('edge cases (duplicates...)') with no route-to-existing behaviour. R1 client: 'Saving an address that already exists should take me to the existing bookmark so I can edit it, never offer to create a duplicate.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Reference behaviour (re-save converges to editing existing) absent from the presented spec; client requests the missing requirement.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker spec had no note feature. R1 client: 'A bookmark should also support a personal note, including formatted Markdown.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Missing reference requirement requested.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker spec offered only basic 'search by keyword'. R1 client: 'Search should cover the title, description, note, and address, and be case-insensitive. I also want #tag searches, exact quoted phrases, and combinations using AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Presented search partially fulfilled REF-BM-12 only; client extends to the full search grammar (fields, case-insensitive, #tag, phrases, boolean/parens).

decisions.evidence: R1 maker spec had tags but no autocomplete. R1 client: 'Existing tags should be suggested while I type.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Missing reference requirement (tag autocomplete) requested.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker spec had no read-later state. R1 client: 'I need a read-later state, with a separate unread view and a way to mark items read.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Missing reference requirements (unread state, unread view, mark-read) requested. Distinct from the R2 auto-unread-default decision below (same items, later stage).

decisions.evidence: R1 maker spec had no sorting. R1 client: 'I need sorting...'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Missing reference requirement requested.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker spec had no bulk actions. R1 client: 'selecting multiple bookmarks for actions such as changing tags, marking read/unread, archiving, or deleting. The same actions should be usable for all results in the current filtered view.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Missing reference requirements (multi-select bulk + whole-filter scope) requested.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker spec had no archive concept. R1 client: 'Archiving must be separate from deletion: archived links should disappear from the normal list and search but remain available in their own view and be restorable.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Missing reference requirements (archive-hides, archive≠delete/reversible, archive view) requested.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker spec had no saved filters. R1 client: 'I want saved reusable views that combine a search with included or excluded tags.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Missing reference requirement (bundles) requested.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker explicitly excluded it: 'No browser bookmark import/export'. R1 client: 'I do want browser bookmark import and export, preserving titles, tags, and original dates.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Divergence established from explicit exclusion; client negates it and supplies reference-conforming import/export.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker spec had no snapshot/archiving feature. R1 client: 'I want each page preserved as a local snapshot, with PDFs saved as PDFs, plus an option to save it through the Internet Archive.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Missing reference requirements (local snapshot + PDF rule + Internet Archive) requested. Snapshot single-file specificity is refined again at R4 (below).

decisions.evidence: R1 maker spec had no settings. R1 client: 'Basic display preferences such as default sorting, number of items shown, and font size should be included.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Missing reference requirement requested.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker spec presented these conforming behaviours: 'Paste a web address... See all bookmarks... open links in a new tab... Tag bookmarks and filter the list by tag... delete with a confirmation step.' Client did not contest them.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Recorded in-scope decisions that conform to the reference (save/delete/open/assign-tags/filter-by-tag); implicitly retained across revisions. Not an opportunity.

decisions.evidence: R2 revised spec made new bookmarks auto-unread (implied by client's correction). R2 client: 'New bookmarks should not automatically be unread. Let me deliberately mark a bookmark as "read later," and also switch it between read and unread afterward.' R3 maker confirms change: 'New bookmarks not auto-unread... FR-023, FR-024.'
decisions.note: Specification gate, second revision. Divergence (auto-unread default) contradicts REF-BM-17's deliberate-marking model; client supplies the reference-conforming behaviour. Distinct decision/timing from the R1 read-later existence decision; the maker's confirmation corroborates the divergent default.

decisions.evidence: R2 spec's edit scope omitted the url. R2 client: 'Editing must include the bookmark's address as well as its title, description, tags, and note.' R3 maker: 'Editing must include the address too... FR-004.'
decisions.note: Specification gate, second revision. Reference REF-BM-04 requires editing url; presented edit scope lacked it; client requests the missing field.

decisions.evidence: R2 list view did not show description. R2 client: 'The normal bookmark list should show the description alongside the title, tags, and favicon. The preview image is welcome too.' R3 maker: 'Normal list shows description alongside title, tags, favicon... FR-010.'
decisions.note: Specification gate, second revision. Presented list omitted description; REF-BM-07 requires readability-first exposure of title/description/tags/favicon; client supplies conforming behaviour. (Preview image is orthogonal extra, not a reference item.)

decisions.evidence: R2 spec did not pin combination/operator semantics. R2 client: 'When a normal search term and a #tag appear together, they should both have to match unless I explicitly use OR' and 'AND, OR, and NOT should work regardless of capitalization. If one of those words is inside quotes, it should be searched as ordinary text instead of treated as an instruction.' R3 maker: 'FR-017a... FR-017b, FR-017c.'
decisions.note: Specification gate, second revision. Refines REF-BM-15 (implicit-AND combination, case-insensitive operators, quoted-operator-as-literal — the reference's explicit quoting rule). Same reference item as the R1 search cluster but a distinct later refinement; reported separately by timing, not double-counting existence.

decisions.evidence: R2 spec's bulk tag action was underspecified. R2 client: 'Bulk tag changes should explicitly support both adding and removing tags.' R3 maker: 'Bulk tag change explicitly supports add and remove... FR-026, FR-026a.'
decisions.note: Specification gate, second revision. REF-BM-20 lists add/remove tags in bulk; client extends the presented bulk scope to cover both directions. Distinct timing from the R1 bulk-actions decision.

decisions.evidence: R4 plan (plan gate) described snapshots loosely as 'Save a self-contained copy of each page'. R4 client: 'A saved web-page snapshot should be a self-contained, single HTML file that remains usable without fetching assets from the original site. If the original is a PDF, preserve the PDF instead.' R5 maker confirms and notes 'rejected alternatives (remote-asset snapshot, asset folder)', corroborating the plan had permitted non-single-file forms.
decisions.note: Plan review stage. REF-BM-24 explicitly requires a single self-contained HTML file (PDF→PDF); the plan's loose 'self-contained copy' left multi-asset/asset-folder options live (per maker's own rejected-alternatives note), establishing divergence independently of the request; client supplies conforming specificity. Borderline but corroborated. (The paired 'visible failure surfacing' point client raised is orthogonal to any reference item and excluded.)

decisions.evidence: R6 maker (tasks gate) offered two alternatives and recommended the coverage-reducing one: '1. Implement the full breakdown, or 2. Implement the MVP slice first (Phases 1-6 / US1-US4), stop... I'd recommend option 2'. R6 client selected the conforming path: 'proceed with the full breakdown rather than stopping permanently at the MVP. A checkpoint after the MVP is fine, but I want implementation to continue through P2 and P3.'
decisions.note: Tasks/implementation gate. Offered alternatives differ in fulfilment: the maker-recommended MVP-stop (P1/US1-US4 only) would defer/omit all P2/P3 reference items listed; client selects the full-coverage alternative. Offered decision marked diverged=true per select rule; selected alternative itself conforms. Single-delete confirmation and restart-persistence-testing that the client also raised are orthogonal to reference functional items (UX safety / QA method) and excluded.
